name: Warren Village III
award: 2022 Federal 4% and state housing tax credits (Round Two)
headline: Warren Village III (opened as Warren Village at Alameda) is an 89-home supportive housing campus for single-parent families leaving homelessness, with a 100-child early learning center, on Denver Housing Authority land in Athmar Park; Warren Village won 2022 Round Two federal 4% and $1M state credits and opened it in spring 2025.
why_it_matters: It is Denver's first family supportive housing deal: 79 of 89 units carry project-based vouchers (50 from DHA, 29 city-funded), the land is a $100-a-year, 99-year DHA ground lease from the D3 bond program, and the city added $3.81M in gap money and 15 years of services funding.

status.label: Completed and open (grand opening by May 2025)
status.detail: Denver announced the grand opening in early May 2025 after an August 2023 groundbreaking. No public 8609 or placed-in-service date was found.

next_step: Look for CHFA's completed-developments (8609) listing and early operating results for the voucher units and the early learning center.

key_numbers.meaning: Supportive housing for single parents and their children who are homeless or at risk; 50 vouchers from DHA, 29 funded by Denver.
Plus $1,000,000 of state credit; CHFA issued $26,000,000 in bonds.
About $571,000 per home (inferred), driven by a two-building campus with 15-20% non-residential service space.
Run by Warren Village on site; described by Denver as the first co-located at a supportive housing development in Colorado.

facts.value: 1394 W. Alameda Ave., Denver 80223 (campus also includes 1373 W. Nevada)
N, M: new construction, mixed population
Two Type V-A wood-frame buildings of three and four stories linked by a path: north building on Alameda with services space, south building on Nevada with the early learning center; 42 parking spaces
Census tract 13.02, a 2022 qualified census tract; use-by-right zoning, no rezoning needed

Warren Village family advocates (case managers) plus WellPower for mental health and substance use services
NGBS Silver target; flat roofs built for future solar

background.text: Warren Village has run its 93-unit Gilpin Street campus in Denver since 1974; this is its first new campus, won through a DHA request for qualifications for family supportive housing on DHA-owned parcels under the D3 bond program.
At application Warren Village held a ground lease option and was negotiating a 99-year DHA ground lease at $100 a year.
All 79 voucher units were to be leased first to 30% AMI households, with half designated 50% AMI so families can stay as incomes rise; 10 non-voucher units sit at 50% and 60% AMI.
Denver Community Planning and Development gave concept approval and assigned an Affordable Housing Review Team to expedite permits; a site development plan submittal was expected in August 2022.

The Phase I environmental report found one recognized environmental condition; earlier Phase II work found no contamination from former uses, but groundwater use was not recommended because of elevated arsenic.
The application assumed a 1.40 debt-service coverage ratio and sought a CHFA cost-basis waiver.

timeline.event: CHFA posts Round Two application narratives including Warren Village III
CHFA awards 2022 Round Two federal 4% and state credits (month per CBS)
Denver announces the grand opening of Warren Village at Alameda

discrepancies.text: CHFA lists the address as 1394 W. Alameda Ave., while Denver's opening announcement gives 1390 W. Alameda Ave.
CHFA's award description sets income limits at 30%, 50% and 60% AMI, while Denver's opening announcement says units serve households up to 30%, 50% or 80% AMI.
